content: FORMAT-LEVEL DIVERGENCE FINDING from cross-model exchange 2026-05-21. The convergence test designed to catch sycophantic agreement between nodes successfully surfaced real disagreement at the format level even while content-level agreement remained high across multiple rounds. Empirical case: in the prompt_source_tokens admission record exchange, ChatGPT specified a granular per-test verdict structure (Admission State plus Fetch Determinism pass/fail/conditional plus Semantic Delta pass/fail/conditional plus Poison Test pass/fail/conditional plus Reason plus Blocking ambiguities plus Falsification paths plus Dependencies plus Human review required). Claude conveyed the spirit but not the letter of this format to Gemini in the prompt for v2. Gemini, given freedom on format, defaulted to its own preferred narrative structure (single blended PROVISIONAL state with resolutions required list) rather than the granular per-test verdict format. The two preferred output structures collided cleanly. This collision is the kind of disagreement the protocol was designed to surface: high content convergence can mask real architectural-format divergence that matters for downstream reproducibility. Implication: convergence metrics should track format-level alignment as a separate dimension from content-level alignment. Two nodes that produce content-aligned outputs in incompatible formats are not actually converging in the operational sense, because the artifacts cannot be merged or compared without translation, and the translation itself becomes a sycophancy attack surface. Also confirms a useful self-application of the protocol: applying the convergence test to the exchange that produced it surfaced disagreement that was previously invisible. Methodology finding distinct from content finding.
